subject: Atlas Pilot: validation checkpoints, conformance tests, and cutover timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@atlasretail.com>, Alejandra Lopez <alejandra.lopez@atlasretail.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Pilot: validation checkpoints, conformance tests, and cutover timeline

Hi Samira / Alejandra —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and a companion acceptance-test checklist for the Atlas pilot. This message summarizes the proposed exit gates and the tests we recommend running during the 4-week evaluation window. Please review and flag anything important we should add.

High-level success criteria (proposed):
- Functional parity for core flows (product search, personalization suggestions, and checkout assistance) — all flows exercised with sampled traffic and regression <2% vs baseline.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 120ms for 99% of pilot traffic (target: 100ms p95 for production if pilot traffic is stable).
- Quality: end-to-end relevance score (internal weighted metric) >= 0.92 on the Atlas eval set; manual spot-check pass rate >= 95%.
- Security / compliance: SOC 2 controls validated for the pilot dataset, and data residency kept within us-east for customer-managed keys.

Proposed exit gates (ordered):
1) Stability gate — 24h without service errors > 0.5% and no model OOMs during peak traffic tests.
2) Quality gate — evaluation run on the provided golden prompts meets quality thresholds above.
3) Ops gate — successful Canary (1% traffic) with automated rollback & monitoring hooks in place.

Acceptance tests (examples, see attached .md for full list):
- Automated functional test suite (50 scripted journeys) passing end-to-end on staging mirror data.
- Load test: sustained 2x expected pilot throughput for 30 minutes without p95 degradation beyond 1.5x baseline.
- Regression eval: compare top-10 hit rate on curated test set.
- Security checklist: KMS integration verified, audit log visibility, and retention policy validated.

Timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP and sign-off on test cases + provide access details.
- Week 1: model onboarding + baseline measurement.
- Week 2: run functional and regression tests; iterate on prompt set.
- Week 3: Canary (1%) + observability burn-in.
- Week 4: Full pilot ramp decision / cutover planning.

Attachments: atlas-map-v1.xlsx (MAP milestones & owners), atlas-acceptance-tests-v1.md (test cases and pass criteria).

Ask: please confirm by EOD Wednesday whether we should: (A) accept these exit gates as-is, (B) add any regulatory constraints (data residency is already noted), or (C) shift latency targets lower/higher for the pilot.

Thanks —
Sooj

Soojinn Lee (she/her)
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Atlas Pilot: validation checkpoints, conformance tests, and cutover timeline

Sooj —

Thanks for the detailed plan. Overall this looks good and aligns with our internal objectives. Quick notes from our side:

- Please add a non-functional exit gate for data residency and encryption-at-rest — we need confirmation KMS keys will stay under our control in us-east for the duration of the pilot.
- SOC 2 evidence: our InfoSec team will require a document listing the specific control owners and where audit logs are stored; can you include a short SOC2 evidence packet?
- Latency: we are comfortable with the 120ms p95 pilot SLO, but would like the roadmap to production to show how you plan to reach 100ms p95. That may affect our acceptance for go-live.
- Procurement: procurement needs a finalized SOW with billing cadence by Apr 5 to meet our internal quarter close.

We are ok to proceed with the timeline but would prefer to push the full pilot ramp by one week if SOC2 packaging or procurement review extends.

Would you and your engineering lead be available Thu 24 March 09:30 PT for a short call to align on the load test parameters and KMS workflow?

Thanks —
Samira
VP of Product, Atlas Retail
samira@atlasretail.com

Sooj / Jordan —

Quick reply before the Thu sync:

- Latency: 120ms p95 for pilot traffic is feasible if Atlas' payloads average <= 1024 tokens and we use the recommended sequence-length trimming on the preprocessor. For production 100ms p95 we should plan for sharded inference nodes and a small token-aware cache. I'll attach a short test harness and a suggested canary policy.
- Acceptance-test harness: I can supply a k6-based load script + a ci/cd job that will run the regression eval and functional journeys against the staging endpoint. This will produce a pass/fail report artifact for the MAP.
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide a minimal packet: (1) control-owner list, (2) last 30-day audit-log extract (redacted), (3) KMS proof-of-ownership doc. I will package these as a PDF and drop it in the shared Drive by Thu EOD.

Edge case: if Atlas wants quantized variants for cost reasons, we should add a performance regression gate (compare quantized vs float baseline) as part of acceptance.

I'll be on the Thu 09:30 call and will share the test harness repo link then.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the items sent to the Drive. Our InfoSec reviewed the SOC2 packet and the KMS proof — acceptable for pilot. Procurement confirmed they can issue a 1-month SOW with net-30 billing if we have the finalized milestones by Apr 5.

- Target pilot cutover window request: Apr 18–22 (Atlas internal calendar) — please confirm Redwood availability for cutover support.
- Please send final SOW draft and DocuSign link by Apr 5.

If all that lands, consider this "approved to proceed" for the pilot kick-off.
